Alright, let me think this through for the year ahead.

I farm 225 mu in Quzhou — that is a serious operation for one household of four. I cannot manage every mu by hand, so I think in terms of blocks and contract some machinery services for ploughing and harvest. Four years is not long, but I read, I talk to the agricultural station in town, and I compare input prices from two dealers in Quzhou before I buy.

**Land allocation.** My main system is wheat-maize double cropping — that's what the soil and irrigation here are set up for. I put 150 mu into the wheat-maize rotation: 150 mu winter wheat from October to June, then immediately 150 mu summer maize from June to October on the same ground. The remaining 75 mu I keep in cotton — my father grew cotton on that block, the ground is sandier there and it does not drain as well for wheat. Cotton also spreads my risk; if wheat price drops I still have cotton.

**Wheat (150 mu, winter).** I use improved variety — Jimai 22 or similar, certified seed, about 12-13 kg/mu seeding rate. Base fertilizer before sowing: compound 15-15-15 at around 40 kg/mu, then urea topdress at green-up and jointing. Total N roughly 16 kg/mu, P 7 kg/mu, K 6 kg/mu. I irrigate 4 times — pre-sowing, green-up, jointing, grain-filling — well water is reliable here. Pesticide 3 times: one for weeds in spring, one for aphids and powdery mildew around heading, one for fusarium head blight if weather turns wet. Rotary tillage after maize stubble — saves diesel vs deep plough and keeps the schedule tight. I target 520 kg/mu; last year I got around 500, the variety and rates should push it.

**Maize (150 mu, summer).** Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Denghai type, planted immediately after wheat harvest — no-tillage direct seeding into wheat stubble saves 7-10 days, which matters for grain filling before autumn cold. N about 18 kg/mu split between base and big-flare stage, P 5 kg/mu, K 5 kg/mu. I irrigate 2 times — after sowing if dry, and at tasseling. Pesticide 2 times: one for corn borer at whorl stage, one for armyworm if scouting shows them. Target 600 kg/mu.

**Cotton (75 mu, spring).** Improved Bt variety to cut bollworm sprays. Transplanting is too much labor at 75 mu so I direct seed with plastic mulch in April. N 17 kg/mu, P 7 kg/mu, K 9 kg/mu — cotton needs more potassium for boll development. Irrigate 3 times. Pesticide is the big cost here — 5 applications for aphids, mites, and late-season bollworm even with Bt. Plough the cotton ground because the residue is woody and rotary does not handle it well. Target 260 kg/mu seed cotton.

**Budget logic.** At 225 mu I cannot afford to skimp on N for wheat and maize — a 50 kg/mu yield loss across 150 mu is far more than the cost of an extra bag of urea. But I also do not over-apply the way my uncle does; I learned in training that excess N on wheat causes lodging, and I saw it happen to him two years ago.
